name: save-buffer-clear-bridge-and-count
body: Two limits. (1) `save` calls `self.buffer.clear()`, and that call is load-bearing now that durability lives in the pending-removal ledger: the list is what admission reads to tell a never-durable identity from a durable one, so an entry surviving the durability boundary would make a later `rm` of an identity saved in this run read as created-this-run, drop its removal, and leave behind the file `save` just made durable — the save derives its delete set from the ledger alone, which never received that identity. Drop the call only when the list itself is removed, never as a tidy-up of the durability point. (2) The save's stdout count (`Session saved: N change(s) in one commit`) is pinned by two e2e tests — `save_flushes_the_buffer_in_one_commit` and `save_on_a_clean_buffer_is_a_noop` — so a reworded count must update them with it.
